headline: Election day opens with tech in a correction, Apple and Palantir lower after beats, oil bouncing on a reported US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, and no put idea passing today's screen: APH is dropped.
summary: The dashboard is current on Monday Nov 2 closes (prices_as_of 2026-11-02), and Massive's Nov 2 closes match it. Monday faded: SPY fell 0.48% to 752.10 and QQQ 1.36% to 681.09, while Lumentum lost 18.6% and Marvell 12.7% on the deal, and Reuters says the Nasdaq 100 closed more than 10% below its record, a correction. Apple and Palantir both beat after the close but fell before the open today (Apple about 4.5% on a margin warning from memory costs, Palantir about 6.3%, Reuters). Brent settled at $104.77 on Monday, down 7.6%, then rose to about $105.77 after the Wall Street Journal reported a US strike on Qeshm Island, even as Trump wrote that Iran wants a settlement. The RBA hiked to 4.85% overnight. Results of today's midterms arrive tonight Eastern time. The put screen found no passing idea: APH left 'Buy zone now' because it fell 8.2% in a month, so the APH idea is removed.

regime.why: Monday's opening bounce failed and tech closed at the lows, with the Nasdaq 100 now in a correction (Reuters). Even good earnings are being sold: Apple and Palantir beat and still fell before the open. Rates are not helping: the RBA hiked again, the Bank of England is expected to hike Thursday, and the new Fed chair warned that rates 'get in the cracks' of AI stocks. The election, a possible Iran escalation and Friday's jobs report all land this week.

signals.title: Midterms today: what each outcome would mean for her themes
signals.since_yesterday: Final forecasts: Decision Desk HQ gives Democrats about 84% odds for the House and 65% for the Senate; Kalshi traders price 94% and 78%.
signals.what_happened: Voting is under way. Republicans hold the Senate 53 to 47 and the House 219 to 214 going in (NBC New York). Decision Desk HQ's model, updated Nov 2, gives Democrats about an 84% chance to win the House and 65% for the Senate; Kalshi's market shows 94% and 78% (Nov 2 to 3). Forecasts agree on the House and differ on the Senate, so the Senate is the swing result. Results come in tonight Eastern time and some races may take days.
signals.so_what: Three outcomes, with what analysts said before the vote. 1) Republicans keep both chambers: RBC saw a modest positive bias for stocks. Policy stays as is: tariffs stay, defense and AI build spending continue. 2) Democrats take the House only: RBC saw a neutral effect. Gridlock means few new laws but more hearings and oversight; Morgan Stanley says defense, technology and financials tend to do fine in divided government, since defense spending has support from both parties. 3) Democrats take both: RBC saw a modest negative bias. A State Street strategist (via Quartz) expects some health stocks to gain if Democrats roll back health spending cuts, which points at Medicaid insurers like MOH and CNC, and consumer staples to gain if tariffs are cut. Evercore ISI warned AI hearings could add risk, though analysts doubt any law would stop the data center build. Crypto rules not yet in law are the most exposed (CNBC, Nov 2). Morgan Stanley's advice is the useful one: the business cycle, earnings and AI spending matter more than the vote. What would make this wrong: a result that takes days to call, which leaves the uncertainty in place.
signals.for_you: Swing: no new swings before results are known; Wednesday's open will gap on the result. Puts: none on defense, managed care or crypto names until Wednesday. Long term: no verdict changes from a vote alone. LMT stays 'Accumulate on pullback', COIN 'Avoid'.

signals.title: Iran: Trump says a deal 'could happen' while the US reportedly struck Qeshm Island; oil bounces after a 7.6% drop
signals.since_yesterday: The Wall Street Journal reported a US strike on Qeshm Island on Monday, and Brent settled at $104.77, down 7.6%, its biggest drop since July.
signals.what_happened: Brent settled at $104.77 on Monday, down 7.6%, and WTI at $96.46, down 7.3% (NBC). Late Monday the Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials, that the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz, home to a missile site, a naval base and a desalination plant; Iranian state media reported five explosions. The Journal called it one of a series of small, unannounced strikes meant to stop attacks on ships, not a restart of the big campaign (France 24, CNBC). The US had not confirmed it. Trump wrote that 'Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible. It could happen!' and told Axios he is 'in no rush' to resume strikes (CBS). Iran's president said Iran's September plan could be carried out in 'two days', including reopening Hormuz, and Qatari mediators flew to Tehran Monday night (Al Jazeera). Brent was about $105.77 Tuesday morning (CNBC) and WTI $98.26, up 1.87% (TipRanks).
signals.so_what: Both tracks are now running at once: small strikes and talks. That is why oil swings 7% on a headline. Who gets paid: tanker owners and US producers while Hormuz stays mostly shut; who pays: airlines and fuel buyers. What becomes scarce is safe passage, not oil in the ground. The tell is whether Iran answers Qeshm with an attack on ships. A real Hormuz deal would take a large part of the war premium out quickly, as Monday showed. Airlines are left out of both lists: Monday's oil drop helped them and today's bounce hurts them, so the direction is unclear until the talks or the strikes win.
signals.for_you: Swing: oil names are a stop management job, not an add. XOM touched its 183.99 target only at Monday's open (high 184.59) and closed at 179.67; CVX never reached its 233.79 target (high 233.25) and closed at 227.77. Keep stops at least at the entries (169.99 and 218.23). COP 146.84 (stop 135.75) and EOG 157.89 (stop 147.98) are still open; no adds. Puts: no puts on energy or airlines this week.

signals.title: Apple and Palantir beat, but both fall before the open: costs and slowing deals
signals.since_yesterday: Results are out: Apple beat on sales and profit but guided margins down on memory costs; Palantir beat and raised but fell on slower US commercial bookings.
signals.what_happened: Apple's fiscal Q4 revenue was $114.4 to $114.5 billion against about $112.95 billion expected, with EPS of $2.10 against $1.98, and iPhone revenue of $57.6 billion, up 17% (Zacks, Motley Fool, Nov 2). Gross margin fell to 47.9% from 50.1%, and Apple guided it to about 45.5% this quarter because of memory chip costs (Motley Fool, Nov 3). Apple fell about 4.5% before the open (Reuters). Palantir's Q3 revenue was $2.31 billion, up 95.9%, and EPS $0.44, both above estimates, and US commercial revenue of $984 million passed government revenue for the first time (Zacks, Motley Fool). It fell about 6.3% before the open (Reuters); a Motley Fool summary links the drop to US commercial contract bookings growth of 6% against 49% in Q2. Zacks gives revenue of $2.31 billion in one note and $2.38 billion in another; the $2.31 billion figure matches Reuters coverage and is used here.
signals.so_what: Two lessons. First, memory is now the chokepoint that takes margin from device makers: Apple paying more is Micron and SK hynix getting paid. Second, after a 10% drop in the Nasdaq 100, the market is selling beats when the next number slows. Expensive stocks need perfect quarters. AMD reports tonight after the close (consensus EPS $1.95 on $13.09 billion, TipRanks).
signals.for_you: No action. AAPL (338.32 on Nov 2, zone 199.95 to 270.52) and PLTR (178.34, zone 69.52 to 94.05) are both Wait. AMD is 'Accumulate on pullback'; no trade into its report tonight.

signals.title: Put screen: APH leaves 'Buy zone now', so the APH put idea is removed; nothing passes today
signals.what_happened: The 'Buy zone now' list shrank from ten names to four on Nov 2 closes: NICE, MSFT, AFRM and COF. APH moved to 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' because it is down 8.2% in a month (79.84, zone 72.99 to 83.83). PODD, RELY, ZTS, PYPL and BLK moved to 'Accumulate on pullback' after bouncing more than 8% above their 50 day averages. Of the four, NICE reports Nov 4 and AFRM Nov 5, so they drop out. MSFT's Dec 11 $420 put last traded at $1.30 on Nov 2 on 2 contracts, about 3.0% annualized, under the 4.91% 10 year. COF's Dec 11 $190 put did not trade on Nov 2. For the record, APH's Dec 18 $72.50 put last traded at $2.15 on Nov 2 on only 43 contracts, with a day range of $1.25 to $2.15 (Massive).
signals.so_what: The rule is doing its job. APH's put still pays well on paper (about 24% annualized at the last trade, about 14% at the day's low), but a stock that fell 8% in a month is the kind that keeps falling through a zone. The thin volume also means the last trade says little. The dashboard's live quote agrees on the price ($2.15) and itself flags the market as thin, with a 19% spread.
signals.for_you: Puts: no new put today; research/put_ideas.json is now empty. If you sold an APH put on yesterday's idea, roll rules apply only near expiry; nothing to do now. APH comes back when its one month drop is under 8% again. Long term: MSFT (507.12) and COF (210.77) are the calm 'Buy zone now' names with no report until late January; small first tranche only after the vote.

signals.title: Marvell and Lumentum: the deal closes in early 2028, and Lumentum now trades 11% under the offer
signals.since_yesterday: LITE fell 18.6% and MRVL 12.7% on Monday, leaving an 11.3% gap to the offer; the filing says closing is expected in the first half of 2028.
signals.what_happened: MRVL closed at 171.41, down 12.7%, on 61.5 million shares, and LITE at 684.40, down 18.6% (Massive, Nov 2). At 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, the offer was worth about 771.35 at Monday's close, so LITE trades about 11.3% below it (my calculation). Lumentum's filing says closing is expected in the first half of calendar 2028, after shareholder and regulatory approvals (SEC 8-K). The filing values the deal near $100 billion; CNBC's $115 billion figure included debt and used earlier prices. The SEC filing is the stronger source and both are noted. Peers fell too: CIEN 11.3% and COHR 4.9% (Massive).
signals.so_what: An 11% gap with a fixed share ratio says traders doubt the deal will close on time, or at all, over a 15 to 18 month review that likely includes China. It also means LITE now moves with MRVL, so it no longer tracks the optics story on its own. Marvell holders are paying for the deal with their own shares.
signals.for_you: No action. MRVL is Wait and below its 218.02 zone floor; LITE is buyout pending. No puts in either.

signals.title: The RBA hiked to 4.85%, the highest since 2008; Copom tomorrow, BoE Thursday
signals.what_happened: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate 0.25 point to 4.85% at 2:30pm Sydney time Tuesday (10:30pm ET Monday) on a 6 to 3 vote, its fifth hike this year, citing inflation, the Middle East war and oil (ABC). Governor Bullock said the bank is 'preserving our options' (Standard Chartered via FXStreet). Brazil's Copom decides Wednesday; a prediction market had 84.5% odds of a hold at 13.75% on Nov 2 (Rio Times). Markets price a Bank of England hike to 4.0% from 3.75% on Thursday at 7am ET (Tradingpedia).
signals.so_what: Central banks outside the US are still hiking because oil keeps inflation up. The split vote at the RBA says the end is near there, but not yet. Rising rates abroad keep pressure on long dated assets like expensive tech, which matches Monday's tape.
signals.for_you: No action. No Brazil or Australia trades. Puts must beat the 4.91% 10 year.

cycle.quadrant_why: Nothing in the data changed the season since Monday: Q3 US GDP grew at a 3.4% pace and core PCE was 3.1% (Oct 29 data), and the RBA hiked on Tuesday citing inflation and oil (ABC). Oil's 7.6% drop on Monday is the one force pushing inflation down, and it is already bouncing.
cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Tightening, late. The RBA hiked to 4.85% on a split vote, the BoE is expected to hike Thursday, and Fed Chair Warsh warned that rates 'get in the cracks' of AI stocks, with hikes expected from December (Motley Fool, Nov 3). The 10 year was 4.91% on Nov 2.
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. Coverage of Warsh's remarks ties high long rates to US debt above $40 trillion (Motley Fool, Nov 3). AI builders now fund spending with stock (Oracle, Marvell).
cycle.big_cycle: Internal order: the midterm vote today. External order: small US strikes and peace talks with Iran at the same time. Technology: the AI trade is in a correction as costs (memory) and funding (stock sales) bite.
tailwinds: Oil is about 7% below last week's level on peace talk hopes.
Earnings are still beating: Apple, Palantir and Lattice all topped estimates.
headwinds: The Nasdaq 100 is in a correction and beats are being sold.
Three central banks lean toward or have delivered hikes this week.

history.what: The Fed was raising rates and shrinking its balance sheet, tech led a fall that began in October, the Nov 6 midterms split Congress, and by Dec 24, 2018 the Nasdaq sat 22% below its August record while the S&P 500 entered a bear market (NBC, Dec 24, 2018).
history.lesson: The vote was not the driver; tightening was. Watch the central banks this week more than the election map.
